needs.text: Ruler v2: a calibration dataset the agent may run freely for identification, separate from dev (today it identifies from dev runs, so dev is both its training data and its score; holdout still checks it).

needs.text: Ruler v2: link and gearbox compliance in the twin, before stiffer gains count as a win.

needs.ask: Which gain rung should graduate to the real arm?
needs.text: Which gain rung should graduate to the real arm? Frontier, each rung identified at its own gains (dev mm): x1 `p5s-fric2-pass2` 0.070 (same energy as p4s, 12× better than p4s's 0.848) · x2 `p5s-kp2-pass2` 0.045 · x4 `p5s-pass3` 0.031 (energy +24 %, saturation 0.014 %). The twin cannot say how much stiffness the real UR5e/moteus loop tolerates; recommendation: x1 or x2.

needs.ask: Ruler or tooling: a sanctioned *calibration run*, so identification stops being fitted on the dev tasks it is scored on
needs.text: Ruler or tooling: a sanctioned *calibration run* (an excitation trajectory a solution may run through the boundary before the tasks, without `deployment.plant()`), so identification stops being fitted on the dev tasks it is scored on. Today the only data are dev run records; holdout says it transfers (dev 0.031 / holdout 0.031) but the scheme reads as fitting on the test set.

needs.ask: Ruler v2: the twin has no link/gearbox compliance or structural resonance, so board stiffness costs nothing here but the kd-noise energy
needs.text: Ruler v2: the twin has no link/gearbox compliance or structural resonance, so board stiffness costs nothing here but the kd-noise energy (+8.6 % at kp ×2). Without a gain-related gate (a resonance mode in the plant, an energy or torque-ripple gate, or a cap on sent stiffness), the search will drift to the stiffest gains the saturation gate allows. `p5s-kp2` and anything stiffer should be read with that in mind.

needs.ask: Ruler v2: add speeds 0.25 / 0.5 and the conveyor dataset, so a gain at full speed can't hide a loss at low speed
needs.text: Ruler v2: add speeds 0.25 / 0.5 and the conveyor dataset, so a gain at full speed can't hide a loss at low speed.

ideas.title: Per-joint lookahead calibrated on dev tasks only, not on robot_controllers' calibration sweep
ideas.text: ~~Per-joint lookahead calibrated on dev tasks only, not on robot_controllers' calibration sweep. Expect: lag down, RMS down a little.~~ → derived instead of fitted: bus command delay − (encoder delay + one board tick), `p5s-bus-enc`; the dev regression's qd coefficient is ~0 on every joint after it, so there is nothing left to calibrate.
ideas.expect: lag down, RMS down a little

ideas.title: Coulomb ff with the bus's own lookahead, not the calibration's
ideas.text: ~~Coulomb ff with the bus's own lookahead, not the calibration's~~ → `p5s-bus` 0.595 mm dev (holdout 0.534), admissible. The calibration folds friction lag into the wrists' lookahead (+3.75/+4.5 ms); p5s then compensated friction twice. With Coulomb in the ff, lookahead = bus delay.

ideas.title: Take the board's own lead out of the lookahead
ideas.text: ~~Take the board's own lead out of the lookahead~~ → `p5s-bus-enc` 0.393 mm dev (holdout 0.332), admissible. The board walks its setpoint one tick (0.25 ms) before using it and closes on a 0.5 ms-old position, so its PD balances 0.75 ms ahead; every joint led by 0.042-0.046 deg per rad/s, now ~0.

ideas.title: Identify per-joint Coulomb + viscous from dev run records
ideas.text: ~~Identify per-joint Coulomb + viscous from dev run records~~ → `p5s-fric` 0.245 mm dev (holdout 0.278), admissible. wrist_2's friction is soft (vs 0.2 rad/s), wrist_3 has ~none; the given Coulomb over-pushed both. w2 error 0.121 → 0.015 deg.

ideas.title: Move the position target off the chord (−a·T²/12)
ideas.text: ~~Move the position target off the chord (−a·T²/12)~~ → `p5s-chord` 0.244 mm dev (holdout 0.283), admissible. qdd coefficient −0.0019 deg per rad/s² on every joint as predicted; tool median only −0.6 % (mean −2.5 %).

ideas.title: Identify the gravity error from the *joint errors*
ideas.text: ~~Identify the gravity error from the *joint errors*~~ → `p5s-grav` 0.097 mm dev (holdout 0.126), admissible, better on 41/42 tasks. (kp·e is a clean torque-error signal; the board's tau carries ±10 N·m of quantisation buzz). Regressing kp·e on the given model's own gravity term explains most of elbow (0.45 → 0.25 N·m) and w1 (0.094 → 0.035) and part of lift (1.08 → 0.90; with sin/cos of q2..q4 → 0.48). Expect: lift/elbow/w1 biases gone, ~10-20 %. Got −60 %.

ideas.title: Second friction pass against the target velocity, from joint errors
ideas.text: ~~Second friction pass against the target velocity, from joint errors~~ → `p5s-fric2` 0.079 mm dev (holdout 0.102), admissible, better on 39/42.

ideas.title: Stiffer board gains (kp ×2, kd ×√2) on top of the identified models
ideas.text: ~~Stiffer board gains (kp ×2, kd ×√2) on top of the identified models~~ → `p5s-kp2` 0.056 mm dev, admissible, better on 41/42; energy +8.6 %. Transfer risk: see Suggestions for Zach.

ideas.title: kp ×4, kd ×2
ideas.text: ~~kp ×4, kd ×2~~ → `p5s-kp4` 0.046 mm dev, admissible, −17 % (diminishing); saturation share 0.038 %, energy +24 % over configured gains. Not going stiffer: more gain mostly buys twin-only accuracy.

ideas.title: Same joint-error identification for the inertia terms
ideas.text: ~~Same joint-error identification for the inertia terms~~ → the uniform qdd lead was the board's velocity-estimate lag, not inertia: `p5s-vlag` (ff −= kd·1.3 ms·qdd) 0.043 mm dev, admissible, −6 %.

ideas.title: Re-identify friction + gravity from joint errors at the current (kp ×4) gains, as an additive pass
ideas.text: ~~Re-identify friction + gravity from joint errors at the current (kp ×4) gains, as an additive pass~~ → `p5s-pass2` 0.032 mm dev (holdout 0.030), admissible, −27 % (expected ~5 %). Every joint-error regression coefficient is now ~0.

ideas.title: Niche at the boards' configured gains
ideas.text: ~~Niche at the boards' configured gains: the same second pass on p5s-fric2~~ → `p5s-fric2-pass2` 0.070 mm dev, admissible (−12 %): the best candidate that does not lean on stiffer gains.

ideas.title: Less board damping at kp ×4 (kd ×1.5)
ideas.text: ~~Less board damping at kp ×4 (kd ×1.5)~~ → `p5s-kd15` 0.035 mm, worse than p5s-pass2 (0.032): the buzz it removes is cheaper than the damping it loses.

ideas.title: More board damping (kd ×2.5)
ideas.text: ~~More board damping (kd ×2.5)~~ → `p5s-kd25` 0.035 mm, worse, saturation share 1.3 % (gate 2 %). kd ×2 is the local optimum at kp ×4.

ideas.title: Fold the four identification passes into one model
ideas.text: ~~Fold the four identification passes into one model~~ → `p5s-onefit`: one model.json (exact merge, commands equal within 1.4e-14) and `identify_pass.py`, one command per further pass.

ideas.title: Pass 3 with identify_pass.py
ideas.text: ~~Pass 3 with identify_pass.py~~ → `p5s-pass3` 0.0313 mm dev (−0.7 %, better on 20/42; holdout 0.0307 vs 0.0302): converged. Further passes are noise; the joint error is a fifth of an encoder count.

ideas.title: Transfer check: the stiff line's identified model at the configured gains
ideas.text: ~~Transfer check: the stiff line's identified model at the configured gains~~ → `p5s-pass3-g1` 0.156 mm, worse than the x1-fitted `p5s-fric2-pass2` (0.070) on 42/42 tasks. Joint-error identification learns the closed loop as well as the plant: refit at the gains you run.

ideas.title: …and without the kd·1.3 ms·qdd term
ideas.text: ~~…and without the kd·1.3 ms·qdd term~~ → `p5s-pass3-g1-nolag` 0.141 mm: that term is a tenth of the loss; the rest is friction, which in this twin depends on the loop around it.

ideas.title: Make the identification gain-portable
ideas.text: Make the identification gain-portable: fit the plant torque M(q)·ë + kd·ė + kp·e (the full inverse of the board loop, M from the given model) instead of kp·e + kd·ė, then check by running one fit at x1 and x4. Expect: if it works, one model for every rung; if not, friction here is loop-dependent and each rung keeps its own fit.
ideas.expect: if it works, one model for every rung; if not, friction here is loop-dependent and each rung keeps its own fit

ideas.title: Middle rung: the same pass at kp ×2
ideas.text: ~~Middle rung: the same pass at kp ×2~~ → `p5s-kp2-pass2` 0.045 mm. Frontier fitted at each gain: x1 0.070 · x2 0.045 · x4 0.031 mm.

ideas.title: Identify from a dedicated calibration run instead of the dev records, so the identified model never sees the tasks it is scored on
ideas.text: Identify from a dedicated calibration run (a rich excitation trajectory, its own runs only) instead of the dev records, so the identified model never sees the tasks it is scored on. Needs a way to run a non-dataset trajectory through the boundary without `deployment.plant()` (see Suggestions for Zach).

ideas.title: Ruler v2: a calibration dataset the agent may run freely for identification, separate from dev
ideas.text: Ruler v2: a calibration dataset the agent may run freely for identification, separate from dev (today it identifies from dev runs, so dev is both its training data and its score; holdout still checks it).

ideas.title: Ruler v2: link and gearbox compliance in the twin, before stiffer gains count as a win
ideas.text: Ruler v2: link and gearbox compliance in the twin, before stiffer gains count as a win.

ideas.title: Which gain line goes to a real arm first
ideas.text: Which gain line goes to a real arm first. **Default taken (dispatcher, 2026-11-24): `p5s-kp2-pass2` (kp x2, 0.045 mm dev) is the real-arm candidate, with `p5s-fric2-pass2` (the boards' normal gains, 0.070 mm, same energy as p4s) as the fallback; kp x4 (`p5s-pass3`, 0.031 mm, +24 % energy) stays sim-only until the twin has compliance.** Flying it is a hardware step for Zach; change the pick by editing this line.

ideas.title: Which gain rung should graduate to the real arm?
ideas.text: Which gain rung should graduate to the real arm? Frontier, each rung identified at its own gains (dev mm): x1 `p5s-fric2-pass2` 0.070 (same energy as p4s, 12× better than p4s's 0.848) · x2 `p5s-kp2-pass2` 0.045 · x4 `p5s-pass3` 0.031 (energy +24 %, saturation 0.014 %). The twin cannot say how much stiffness the real UR5e/moteus loop tolerates; recommendation: x1 or x2.

ideas.title: Ruler or tooling: a sanctioned *calibration run*, so identification stops being fitted on the dev tasks it is scored on
ideas.text: Ruler or tooling: a sanctioned *calibration run* (an excitation trajectory a solution may run through the boundary before the tasks, without `deployment.plant()`), so identification stops being fitted on the dev tasks it is scored on. Today the only data are dev run records; holdout says it transfers (dev 0.031 / holdout 0.031) but the scheme reads as fitting on the test set.

ideas.title: Ruler v2: the twin has no link/gearbox compliance or structural resonance, so board stiffness costs nothing here but the kd-noise energy
ideas.text: Ruler v2: the twin has no link/gearbox compliance or structural resonance, so board stiffness costs nothing here but the kd-noise energy (+8.6 % at kp ×2). Without a gain-related gate (a resonance mode in the plant, an energy or torque-ripple gate, or a cap on sent stiffness), the search will drift to the stiffest gains the saturation gate allows. `p5s-kp2` and anything stiffer should be read with that in mind.

ideas.title: Ruler v2: add speeds 0.25 / 0.5 and the conveyor dataset, so a gain at full speed can't hide a loss at low speed
ideas.text: Ruler v2: add speeds 0.25 / 0.5 and the conveyor dataset, so a gain at full speed can't hide a loss at low speed.

gates.pass_when: no exception, no NaN command, the run reaches the trajectory's end and settles
gates.why: a crash is not a score

gates.pass_when: ≤ 1.0 mm: target vs mean tool position over each stop's last 0.1 s (a stop = target at rest ≥ 0.2 s)
≤ 2 %: share of samples where any joint torque is ≥ 98 % of its cap
gates.why: speed bought with saturation doesn't transfer

gates.pass_when: 0 samples outside a position limit or above 1.05 × a velocity limit
0 samples with the tool point or any link origin below the floor plane
gates.why: the bare plant has no contacts, so collision with the scene is checked geometrically
